title: Distributed Lovász Local Lemma in O(log log n) rounds
formal: Does there exist an integer c≥2 such that, for every fixed integer d≥2, a uniform randomized LOCAL algorithm A_d and a constant K_d solve every n-event variable Lovász Local Lemma instance of dependency degree at most d and maximum bad-event probability p with p·d^c<1/2, within K_d(1+log₂log₂(n+2)) rounds, with probability at least 1−n^(−3) of avoiding all bad events simultaneously?
context:
The target is worst-case round complexity over all nodes. A node-averaged O(log log n) result does not meet it.

This short research proposal states the target identified in the September 2026 fundamental-problem search. The references give the source models and related results. definitions: There are n≥2 bad events, each a predicate on a specified finite subset of finitely many mutually independent variables. Each variable has a finite nonempty alphabet and a rational probability distribution; event predicates and distributions are given by finite tables. Variables occurring in no event can be omitted. Two distinct event nodes are adjacent exactly when their variable sets intersect; this graph is the communication network. Its maximum degree is at most d. The number p is the largest probability of an event under the product of the specified distributions. Each node initially knows n,d, its own event table, its variables and their distributions, its neighbours and their identifiers. Node identifiers are distinct integers in [n²]; shared variables have consistent names. LOCAL means synchronous rounds with arbitrarily long finite messages in each direction on each edge, and unrestricted terminating local computation. Nodes have private independent fair random bits. A single finite program is used at all nodes, independently of n and the instance. Each node outputs one value for each of its variables. Success requires agreement on shared variables and falsity of every event. The round bound holds on every random tape; the success probability is over all node coins for each fixed instance and identifier assignment. Constants and the algorithm may depend on d; the slack exponent c is chosen before d. No preprocessing using the full instance is supplied. The factor 1/2 removes the low-degree ambiguity recorded in the source conjecture.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

notes: Replaced sufficiently strong slack and high probability by quantified constants; specified the finite variable setting, LOCAL inputs and simultaneous output.

sentences: The distributed Lovasz Local Lemma seeks an assignment avoiding many bad events, each depending on only a bounded number of other events.
Processors know local portions of this dependency structure and communicate in synchronous LOCAL rounds.
The question asks for O(log log n) rounds with high probability when the dependency degree is constant and the probability criterion has sufficiently strong constant polynomial slack.
The guarantee must bound the worst finishing time over all nodes.
An algorithm that achieves only a small average finishing time would leave the central coordination issue unresolved for the last remaining bad events.
